beats.narration_text: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. You use Claude at work, and the answers are good. So the real question is not whether to use it. It is what you should never paste into it.

props.text:
Can I paste my work
into Claude?

beats.motion_claim: The writer types the naive paste question and corrects it to the real one: what is confidential.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: Three terms you will need. Training: when a company uses your chats to teach its model. Retention: how long it keeps those chats. And a clean room: a personal rule that sensitive stuff never enters the chat at all.

terms.meaning: a company using your chats to teach its model
how long the company keeps your chats
a rule: sensitive stuff never enters the chat

qc.sparse_reason: TERMS card: three prerequisites, one line each.

beats.narration_text: Picture the scene. You are on a deadline, Claude is open, and the document you need summarized is right there. You paste it in and get your answer in seconds. That paste — quick, harmless-feeling — is what this film is about.

shot.visual_intent: Your chat window; a document slides in from the left and a ring marks the paste.
shot.motion_claim: Your chat window; a document slides in from the left and a ring marks the paste.

beats.narration_text: In April 2023, Samsung let its engineers use ChatGPT. Within about three weeks, three leaks: source code pasted to fix a bug, equipment code pasted to fix a defect, and a whole meeting uploaded for minutes. Samsung banned the tools and warned of disciplinary action.

shot.visual_intent: Three documents drop one by one into a chat window; a ban stamp lands over it.
shot.motion_claim: Three documents drop one by one into a chat window; a ban stamp lands over it.

beats.narration_text: Here is why the paste matters. On a personal Claude plan — Free, Pro, or Max — your chats can train the model, and be kept up to five years. Since September 2025, that training is on by default.

shot.visual_intent: A cable runs from your chat window to a dark training server; its lights come on; a '5 years' tag lands.

show.event: cable draws; server lights come on

shot.motion_claim: A cable runs from your chat window to a dark training server; its lights come on; a '5 years' tag lands.

beats.narration_text: The fix is one toggle. In Claude: Settings, then Privacy, and switch the training toggle off. Do it before your next conversation, not after.

shot.visual_intent: A settings panel; the Privacy row highlights; a cursor flips the training toggle from ON to OFF.
shot.motion_claim: A settings panel; the Privacy row highlights; a cursor flips the training toggle from ON to OFF.

beats.narration_text: The same switch exists everywhere. ChatGPT: Settings, Data controls, turn off Improve the model for everyone. Grok: on X, Settings, Privacy and safety, uncheck training. Gemini: on Google's My Activity page, turn off Gemini Apps activity.

shot.visual_intent: Three app panels — ChatGPT, Grok, Gemini — each with a toggle that flips OFF in turn.
shot.motion_claim: Three app panels — ChatGPT, Grok, Gemini — each with a toggle that flips OFF in turn.

beats.narration_text: One catch: the toggle only works going forward. It cannot pull back anything already used in a training run. So flip it now — not after your next session.

shot.visual_intent: The OFF toggle; an arrow runs forward from it; a sealed box marked 'already used' stays shut.
shot.motion_claim: The OFF toggle; an arrow runs forward from it; a sealed box marked 'already used' stays shut.

beats.narration_text: I am not a lawyer — but a lawyer could frame a paste three ways. Breaking your NDA: the AI company is an outside party. Breaking data protection law, depending on where you live. Or breaking your own company's IT policy.

shot.visual_intent: Three seals stamp down in a row: NDA, data law, IT policy.
shot.motion_claim: Three seals stamp down in a row: NDA, data law, IT policy.

beats.narration_text: So run a clean room. Four things never go into a personal AI account: client names, internal financials, source code, meeting recordings. And anonymize before you paste — swap real names for placeholders.

shot.visual_intent: Four documents each get an X; then one document's real name swaps to a placeholder.

a name swaps to a placeholder

beats.narration_text: And if your company will pay for it: work and enterprise plans do not train on your data at all. If sensitive data is your daily work, that is the plan to ask for.

shot.visual_intent: An office block rises; a shield with a check lands on it: no training.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: Look through our past chats and list every piece of work data I pasted in — names, numbers, code, meetings — and flag what should never have gone in. Then check two things yourself: in Claude, open Settings, then Privacy, and confirm the training toggle is off. And delete any chat holding something confidential.
